attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated as his belief.

semantics.note: He says 'I think' most loans 'end up' underwater, and gives a two-year horizon. I read this as unqualified expectation, not graded probability, so it is a scorable forecast. The drafter's 'likely' modality overstates the hedge. The normalised text drops 'I don't think' on demand but keeps the substance.

contract.note: The plain reading of underwater (principal exceeds collateral value) and of most (over half, reported both by loan count and by principal) is an ordinary, fair reading. The deadline of 2027-12-29 matches the stated two years.

evidence.note: JLL midyear 2026 report puts North American vacancy at 1%. This weighs against a current glut but does not measure loan collateral coverage, and the deadline is still to come.
Bloomberg, 2026-10-28, reports double-digit yields on AI-infrastructure debt. Market stress is not evidence that loans are underwater, and the contract excludes yields as a proxy.

reviews.rationale: This is a forecast due 2027-12-29, which is after the evaluation date. No dated event meets the early-resolution rule: there is no loan-level collateral dataset showing a majority underwater. The vacancy and yield evidence is context only. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion about the seven companies he named just before it.

semantics.note: 'They are all' correctly refers to the seven named firms. 'No path to profitability' is an evaluative judgment folded into a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Choosing Q3 2025 and whole-company net results is a reasonable plain reading, but it is the evaluator's choice. The 'path to profitability' standard was not supplied by the speaker and largely decides any verdict on that part.

evidence.note: The Replit CEO says the company is gross-margin positive. Gross margin does not establish net profit or loss for the target quarter.
An August 2026 report says Lovable was profitable at some earlier, unspecified time, on an unknown basis. It cannot be placed in Q3 2025. It raises caution but does not decide the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no comparable Q3 2025 profit-and-loss records for any of the seven companies. Replit's gross margin and Lovable's undated profitability bear on the claim but do not establish whole-company results in the target period. The 'no path' part has no settled evidence either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own argument in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The causal structure (inherent unprofitability, therefore dependence on venture funding) is kept, along with 'all signs suggest' and the end-points. In context, 'every single company' plausibly means VC-backed AI startups, which is narrower than the contract's population.

contract.note: The reading as continuing venture subsidy is ordinary. The population of all generative-AI model and app businesses may be broader than the speaker meant, given his venture-funding context. The Q3 2025 window is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: TIME (August 2025) says Midjourney became profitable without investors around 2022. This is a different period with no accounting basis, and Midjourney may fall outside the VC-funded scope he had in mind. It is tension, not a decisive counterexample.

reviews.rationale: No matched financial and funding records establish universal dependence on venture funding, or its absence, in Q3 2025. The Midjourney report challenges the universal claim but is outside the period and lacks financial detail. Nothing in the packet separates inherent economics from discretionary growth spending.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own article.

semantics.note: The universal scope, the scale, and the hedged 'only seem to lose it' are all preserved. 'Take forever' is rhetorical. The contract reasonably draws on the article's 1–3 year context for it.

contract.note: Separating arranging from retained exposure, and reading losses as after costs, are fair plain readings. The institution universe and accounting basis are undefined, so interpretation would decide any verdict.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own disclosure lists major banks in a $2.6B syndicate. It does not show each bank's retained amount, and it does not cover every major institution.
CoreWeave's Q3 2025 company-level net loss is $110M. This does not show losses for individual facilities or lenders.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows some major banks taking part in AI data-center financing and one borrower reporting a corporate loss. There is no institution-by-institution exposure data and no project-level record of revenue start dates and later losses. The universal claim is neither established nor refuted.
